title: A finite separable extension making all residue fields of finitely many finite extensions purely inseparable
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $K_1,\dots,K_n$ be finite field extensions of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Then there is a finite field extension $L/k$ which is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] such that for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$: (a) the ring $L\otimes_kK_i$ has only finitely many prime ideals; (b) for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $L\otimes_kK_i$ the quotient $(L\otimes_kK_i)/\mathfrak p$ is a field, and, regarded as an extension of $L$ through $l\mapsto l\otimes1$, it is a finite purely inseparable extension of $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. (One may take for $L$ a finite Galois extension of $k$ into which the separable closures $L_i$ of $k$ in $K_i$ all embed over $k$.)

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (more-morphisms.tex lines 12060-12079: choice of the separable subfields L_i, of a finite Galois L receiving all L_i, and 'by our choice of L (and elementary field theory) we see that kappa(u) subset kappa(y_{i,j}) is finite purely inseparable'); field theory in Fields, Lemma 030K (fields-lemma-separable-first, line 1704), Lemma 09DT (fields-lemma-normal-closure, line 2086) and Lemma 0EXM (fields-lemma-normal-closure-galois, line 2704)
